rationale: No story/spec artifact exists for this sdlc-light run, so this is a genuine no-spec round (confidence forced low per schema). Blind and edge-case lenses both ran. The edge-case lens found one real, testable gap: scoping loadNativeSessions() to filter.sessionId before readPiTranscripts/foldPiForkFamilies silently drops Pi /fork continuation data when the requested sessionId is the fork root, since the continuation (a different sessionId) is filtered out of `scoped` before the fold pass can see it. One additional low-confidence, low-likelihood finding (sessionId collision across agents) is deferred — Claude/Codex/Pi/etc. session IDs are UUID-derived filenames, making a real collision implausible; not blocking. The blind lens's other two concerns (windowDays() returning undefined being a breaking contract, and widening the discovery window increasing memory pressure) were verified against the actual adapter code and discoverSessions() implementations and found to be non-issues: every adapter already falls back to its own `?? 30` default when maxAgeDays is undefined, and discoverSessions() only does readdir/stat (no file-content reads), so widening the window does not reintroduce the OOM. 1 finding emitted (patch), 1 deferred, 0 dismissed.

findings.title: Session-scoped report silently drops Pi fork-continuation data when filter.sessionId targets a fork root
findings.problem: `scoped = discovered.filter(d => d.descriptor.sessionId === filter.sessionId)` is computed before `readPiTranscripts(scoped, deps)` / `foldPiForkFamilies(piTranscripts)` run. When the requested sessionId is the ROOT of a Pi `/fork` family, the fork continuation (which carries a different sessionId and holds all post-fork turns) is excluded from `scoped` before the fold pass ever sees it — unlike the existing 'orphaned fork kept standalone' safety net, there is no equivalent here; the continuation's data is dropped outright, not folded or kept standalone.
findings.impact: A single-session analytics report for a Pi session that was later forked silently undercounts turns/duration/spend for that session, with no error or warning — the exact kind of quiet data-loss this ticket is trying to eliminate, just for Pi forks specifically. Untested: native-loader-pi.test.ts's fork-family tests only call loadNativeSessions(undefined, ...), never with a sessionId filter.
findings.recommendation: Before narrowing to `scoped`, when `filter.sessionId` is set, also include any Pi descriptor whose parsed `parentSession` chain resolves to the matched descriptor (or vice versa) so `readPiTranscripts`/`foldPiForkFamilies` still see the full family for fold purposes, then filter the *output* down to the requested session's synthesized record. Add a test scoping `loadNativeSessions({ sessionId: <fork-root> })` over a discovered root + fork pair asserting the folded result still carries the fork's turns.
